name: REPT
description: REPT repeats a text string a specified number of times and returns the combined result.
tldr: Repeats text a given number of times.

parameters.name: number_times
parameters.description: A positive number indicating how many times to repeat text. Fractional values are truncated to integers.

basicExample.explanation: The string "*- " is concatenated three times.

advancedExamples.title: In-cell bar chart
advancedExamples.scenario: Cell A1 holds a count like 5
advancedExamples.explanation: REPT draws one bar per unit, creating a quick text-based chart without a chart object.

advancedExamples.title: Pad a value with leading zeros
advancedExamples.explanation: REPT creates the needed number of leading zeros, then concatenates the number.

howItWorks: REPT concatenates the text argument to itself number_times times. The repeat count is truncated to an integer, and if it is 0 the result is an empty string.

howToSteps.name: Set the count
howToSteps.text: Provide how many times to repeat it.

limitations: The result is limited to 32,767 characters; longer outputs return #VALUE!.
number_times is truncated to an integer and must be non-negative.
Purely cosmetic; the repeated text is not a real chart or formatted number.

commonErrors.cause: The repeated result would exceed 32,767 characters, or number_times is negative.
commonErrors.fix: Reduce the repeat count so the total length stays under the limit and keep it non-negative.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: REPT works identically in Google Sheets.

faq.question: Can REPT create a bar chart?
faq.answer: Yes, repeating a character like "|" a number of times proportional to a value is a common in-cell chart trick.

faq.question: Is the repeat count rounded?
faq.answer: Fractional counts are truncated to an integer, not rounded.
